sb_prompt: DISCUSS PLANNING A FAMILY REUNION.  DRAW ON YOUR EXPERIENCES AND THOSE OF THE OTHER CALLER FOR MAKING THE NEXT GET-TOGETHER SUCCESSFUL AND MEMORABLE.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Hi, this is Susan. Is this Mary?
ParticipantB: Yeah, it's Mary.
ParticipantA: Hey Mary, thanks for taking my call. I was hoping we could chat about family reunions. I've been thinking a lot about planning one lately.
ParticipantB: Oh, sure. Yeah, that's a good topic. My mom actually just made a big fuss about how we should do one this summer.
ParticipantA: That's great! My aunt tried to organize one last year and it kind of fell apart. Everyone was mad. I know exactly how that goes.
ParticipantB: Oh really? Tell me about that. Did you know my cousin on my mom's side? He had a huge meltdown at the last family thing.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I know him! He's the one who wouldn't RSVP. He showed up two hours late eating a cold pizza in the driveway. My aunt, she cried. She really did.
ParticipantB: Wow, that sounds tough. He's pretty much like that. Always making things awkward. I think that's why my mom is so stressed now. She's trying to figure out how to keep everyone from freaking out.
ParticipantA: That is exactly why I think we need to plan the next one carefully. I have this idea, you know? Maybe we don't invite everyone at once? Like, break it into smaller groups?
ParticipantB: Hmm. I guess that could work. My husband thinks it's a bad idea though. He says family is family, you just get them all in one room.
ParticipantA: But what if we just pick a few families first? Like, my husband's side and my mom's side, but keep them separate for dinner, then mix them for a game or something later?
ParticipantB: Oh, I see. That might actually be good. My sister-in-law always feels left out when it's a huge crowd. She's shy, you know?
ParticipantA: Exactly! And I could make a really nice potluck if we do smaller groups. Everyone brings one dish. I'll bring the salad and the bread.
ParticipantB: That sounds nice. I can bring a casserole. My mom's famous green bean casserole. She's the only one who makes it right.
ParticipantA: Oh, I love green bean casserole! That would be perfect. So, if we split the groups, who would you want to invite first?
ParticipantB: Well, I think I'd want to get the cousins on my dad's side first. They haven't seen each other in years. My uncle Bob is getting pretty old, you know.
ParticipantA: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Is he sick?
ParticipantB: No, just old. And his wife, she's really tight with my mom. If we just have the two of them and a couple of cousins, it won't be so overwhelming.
ParticipantA: That makes sense. I think I'd invite my brother and his family. He lives in the next town over, so it's easy for them.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that could work. Maybe we call them next week? And figure out the date. I know my boss is crazy busy, so I'm not sure when I can get off work.
ParticipantA: Oh, I get it. I work in an office, people think I'm just sitting there all day, but I have to answer phones and stuff. Sometimes I can't just leave if someone needs me.
ParticipantB: Oh, sorry to hear that. I drive a school bus. So I'm on the road all day. Sometimes I don't even get home until after my kids' dinner.
ParticipantA: No way! That's tough. I've heard stories about drivers, but I didn't think you actually drove a bus.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it's a lot. But the kids are good. One of them, actually, her dad has some health issues. She comes to my place sometimes after school to visit.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? That's nice of you. That's a lot of responsibility.
ParticipantB: Yeah. And because of that, I'm a little worried about a big reunion. If everyone comes together and there's drama, like my cousin Bob did last time, I don't think I can handle it.
ParticipantA: I totally get that. Last time my aunt cried because Bob showed up late. It was really hard on her. Maybe doing smaller groups helps avoid that kind of stress.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I think that's the key. If we keep it small, my mom won't be stressed, and my sister-in-law won't feel left out. And we can see how it goes before inviting everyone else.
ParticipantA: That sounds like a solid plan. Maybe we can try just your side of the family first? Like the cousins and your mom?
ParticipantB: Hmm, maybe not my mom. She needs her peace and quiet mostly. How about just the cousins? And maybe one or two aunts?
ParticipantA: Okay, so just the cousins on your dad's side and maybe one aunt? And I'll bring my brother and his family as a separate group?
ParticipantB: Yeah, that sounds manageable. I can talk to my mom and see if she wants to meet them too, but not at the same time.
ParticipantA: And I'll call my brother tomorrow to see if he can make it. He usually does, but he gets busy.
ParticipantB: Okay. Well, thanks for calling. I feel a little less stressed already just talking about splitting it up.
ParticipantA: Yeah, me too. It seems so much easier to manage. Okay, well I gotta run, my line is probably ringing for another caller soon.
ParticipantB: Oh, okay. Good luck with it.
ParticipantA: Thanks, bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
